title: Continental Airlines 603
summary: Continental Airlines Flight 603, a McDonnell Douglas DC-10-10, experienced cascading tire failures during takeoff roll from runway 6R when the recapped tread of the number-two tire on the left main landing gear separated. This caused that tire to blow out, and the overload caused the adjacent number-one tire to blow out immediately. Metal pieces from both rims damaged the number-five tire. Unable to stop on the wet runway, the aircraft overran the departure end and the left main gear collapsed, puncturing fuel tanks and causing a post-impact fire that resulted in four fatalities and moderate injuries to many others.
probable_cause: The probable cause of this accident was the sequential failure of two tires on the left main landing gear and the resultant failure of another tire on the same landing gear at a critical time during the takeoff roll. These failures resulted in the captain's decision to reject the takeoff. Contributing to the accident was the cumulative effect of the partial loss of aircraft braking because of the failed tires and the reduced braking friction achievable on the wet runway surface which increased the accelerate-stop distance to a value greater than the available runway length. This prevented the captain from stopping the aircraft within the runway confines. The failure of the left main landing gear and the consequent rupture of the left wing fuel tanks resulted in an intense fire which added to the severity of the accident.

factors.evidence: Recapping tread of the number-two tire on the left main landing gear separated from the tire causing a blowout; this overload caused the adjacent number-one tire to blow out immediately (p. 5-6). The number-two tire may have been operated in an over-deflection condition due to suboptimal average inflation pressure for maximum gross weight (p. 5).
The aircraft could not stop within the confines of the runway partly because the runway was wet, reducing braking friction from that which would be available on a dry runway (p. 5).

Partial loss of braking power following the failure of the three tires on the left main gear compounded the stopping distance problem (p. 5). Metal pieces from rims of failed tires damaged the number-five tire causing a third blowout on left main gear (p. 5).

Aircraft could not stop within the confines of the runway and overran the departure end by approximately 664 feet; left main gear broke through nonload-bearing pavement, collapsed rearward, and punctured fuel tanks in left wing (p. 5).

Portions of the failed gear punctured fuel tanks in the left wing, immediately starting a fuel fire; intense fire which added to severity of accident with four fatalities and moderate injuries to many occupants (p. 5).

events.text: Flight 603 called Los Angeles clearance delivery and was cleared for the route of flight
Los Angeles ground control gave permission to push back from gate; approximately 2 minutes after clearance delivery
Flight 603 cleared by ground control to taxi to runway 6R; runway was wet but had no standing water
Local control cleared Flight 603 to position on runway 6R and hold for takeoff
Local control cleared Flight 603 for takeoff; flightcrew acknowledged the instructions
Aircraft began takeoff roll with normal acceleration; all engine instruments in normal range
Airspeed approached V1 speed of 156 knots; captain heard loud metallic bang followed by aircraft quivering and left wing drop
Captain rejected takeoff immediately after hearing metallic bang and noting aircraft instability; Digital Flight Data Recorder showed airspeed had increased to approximately 159 knots
Captain applied full brake pressure while bringing thrust levers back to idle power and actuating full reverse thrust
Number-one tire on left main landing gear blew out after number-two tire failure; metal pieces from rims damaged number-five tire causing third blowout
Left main landing gear collapsed after aircraft overran runway end; gear break through nonload-bearing pavement and ruptured left wing fuel tanks
Intense fuel fire erupted from ruptured left wing fuel tanks; aircraft came to rest approximately 664 feet beyond runway departure end

recommendations.text: Require airworthiness directive to inspect tire condition and change tires that show excessive wear or tread separation
Require inspection procedures and standards for recapped tires used on air carrier aircraft
Establish more stringent quality control standards for tire retreading facilities serving air carriers
Require tire pressure monitoring systems to alert flight crews to pressure loss during takeoff
Review and revise aircraft certification standards relating to landing gear and brake failure conditions

safety_changes: Improved tire retreading standards for aircraft
Tighter quality control for aircraft tire manufacturers
Better tire pressure monitoring systems for takeoff
